title: Verity Rail Company
description: The corporate web site of Verity Rail Company, a regional freight railroad, unchanged since June 2011 when it conveyed the last of its Verity County branch corridors to the county.

blocks.text: VERITY RAIL COMPANY  ***  SAFETY IS A CONDITION OF EMPLOYMENT  ***  TO REPORT AN EMERGENCY AT A GRADE CROSSING, CALL THE NUMBER ON THE BLUE AND WHITE SIGN AT THE CROSSING AND GIVE THE CROSSING NUMBER PRINTED ON IT  ***

blocks.caption: VR 2214 southbound at Ardo. Photograph by Company personnel.

blocks.body:
Verity Rail Company is a regional freight railroad. The Company operates 147.4 route miles and interchanges with two Class I carriers, at Steuben and at Ardo Junction.

The Company was formed in 1983 in a regional restructuring and has been a wholly owned subsidiary of [b]Cordray Rail Holdings, Inc.[/b] since November 2004. It operates under its own name, with its own employees and its own operating rules.

Beginning in 2005 the Company undertook a review of its network with the objective of concentrating maintenance and crew resources on the segments that generate sustainable volume. That work is complete.

Network optimization reduced operated mileage by approximately seventeen percent between 2006 and 2009 while retaining, in the Company's assessment, ninety-four percent of originating volume. The segments removed from service were those on which volume had declined to a level at which continued maintenance could not be supported by the traffic. The Company's current service footprint is set out on the [url=/network]Our Network[/url] page.

blocks.body:
Safety is a condition of employment at Verity Rail. The Company recorded [b]1.9[/b] reportable injuries per 200,000 employee hours in 2010, against 2.4 in 2009 and 3.1 in 2006.

The Company's grade crossing inventory, and what to do if your vehicle is stopped on a crossing, are on the [url=/safety]Safety and Grade Crossings[/url] page. Read that page before you need it.

Car orders, demurrage, storage, credit applications and rate quotations are handled by the Marketing Department at Ardo. See [url=/customers]Shipping With Us[/url].

The Company does not accept car orders through this web site and has no plan to. There is no plan because there is no web site budget; the sentence above is the whole of the Company's electronic commerce policy and it has not changed since 2002.

[i]This page was last reviewed on Thursday 3 February 2011.[/i]

The interactive system map requires Adobe Flash Player 9 or later. If the map does not appear, the printable version on the [url=/network]Our Network[/url] page is current to 1998.

Verity Rail operates over one main line, two subdivisions and two industrial tracks. Two further segments in Verity County are no longer in service and are described below for reference, because people continue to ask about them and it is cheaper to write it down once.

blocks.body:
Maximum authorized speed is 40 mph on the Ardo Main Line, 25 mph on the Halsey Subdivision and 10 mph on the industrial tracks. The Company operates by track warrant control on the main line and by yard limits elsewhere. Road communication is on [b]160.590 MHz[/b], AAR channel 30.

Marchfield is an open station on the Halsey Subdivision at MP 22.8 and remains open. Marchfield is not closed. This is stated here because the Company is asked otherwise about twice a month.

blocks.caption: System map, 1998 printing, scanned 2002. No later edition was printed. Both Verity County branches are shown as in service, which they were when the map was drawn.

blocks.body:
The Gridfall Subdivision runs 18.4 miles from Ardo Junction to the Company's yard at Depot Street, Gridfall. It was built in 1899 by the Verity & Ardo Railway to serve the tannery and the grist mills, and came to the present Company in 1983.

Application for authority to abandon was filed in August 2005. Authority was granted in November 2006 after two comment periods and a public hearing. The final scheduled movement left Depot Street on Friday 30 March 2007.

Track remains in place over the entire subdivision. The Company has made no decision regarding salvage and has no plan to restore service. Adjoining landowners were notified in writing in April 2007 and again in September 2009.

blocks.body:
Traffic on the subdivision in its final years was substantially all aggregate from the pit at Quarry Road. The subdivision handled fewer than 400 carloads in 2004.

Sixteen positions were eliminated at closing: eleven in the yard, three on the track gang, two clerical. Nine employees were offered positions on the Ardo Main Line.

The Marchfield Subdivision extended 11.6 miles east from Marchfield to Coyne Flats. Traffic in the final years consisted of grain originating at the elevator east of Marchfield and occasional inbound fertilizer and agricultural chemical at Coyne Flats.

The last revenue movement over the subdivision was on [b]Friday 14 March 2008[/b]: three loaded covered hopper cars of corn from the Marchfield Farmers Cooperative Association elevator, billed to the river terminal at Steuben.

A notice of exemption was filed on 6 June 2008 and the abandonment was consummated on 12 September 2008. Track material was recovered in 2009. The corridor was conveyed to Verity County in June 2011. The whole of it, in the order it happened, is on the [url=/abandonment]Marchfield Subdivision: Discontinuance of Service[/url] page.

blocks.body: The four bridge structures remain in place and were conveyed with the corridor in their condition as inspected in 2009. The Company's inspection reports were furnished to the county engineer at that time and the Company retains no copy.

The Company interchanges at [b]Steuben[/b] and at [b]Ardo Junction[/b]. Interchange is daily except Sunday at Steuben and on call at Ardo Junction.

Truck-competitive movements out of Coyne Flats and Marchfield are brokered through Kroon Trucking, Coyne Flats, whose page is [url=synth://kroontrucking.synth/]here[/url]. The Company has no financial interest in Kroon Trucking and makes nothing on the freight.

Verity Rail is a small railroad and its sales department is four people in one room at Ardo. That is not an apology. It means that if you telephone in the morning you will speak to the person who makes the decision, which is not true of the carriers we interchange with.

Empty supply is quoted in working days and is honest. If the Company cannot spot on the day you ask, you will be told on the day you ask.

The Company operates a transload at Halsey: two spots, paved apron, forklift to 8,000 lb, no crane, no scale of its own. Plastic pellets, lumber, steel and bagged fertilizer move through it. Aggregate does not, and the answer to the next question is also no.

For grain that no longer has rail at origin, the practical arrangement since 2008 has been truck to Halsey. That is worse for the shipper than rail at the elevator door was, and the Company has said so in writing to the two shippers it affects.

blocks.text: Company conveys Marchfield corridor to Verity County -- Friday 17 June 2011

blocks.body:
ARDO -- Verity Rail Company has completed the conveyance of the former Marchfield Subdivision right of way to Verity County.

The conveyance covers 11.2 miles of corridor between Wessel Street, Marchfield, and the end of track at Coyne Flats. The deed was recorded in the office of the county recorder on Thursday 16 June 2011.

The Company retains no interest in the corridor and no responsibility for its maintenance, fencing, mowing, drainage or fire control. Four bridge structures are included and are transferred in their present condition.

The Company's 2009 structure inspection reports have been furnished to the county engineer.

Questions regarding the future use of the corridor should be directed to the Verity County highway department. The Company is not a party to any trail proposal and has no view on one.

Employee timetable No. 14 becomes effective at 0001 on Tuesday 12 April 2011. Timetable No. 13 and all special instructions, bulletins and general orders issued against it are void at that time.

Copies have been distributed to all operating employees and are available at Ardo, Steuben and Halsey. Employees are reminded that possession of a current timetable is a condition of service.

The Gridfall Subdivision and the Marchfield Subdivision do not appear in timetable No. 14.

blocks.text: 2010 operating results reported to parent -- Thursday 3 February 2011

blocks.body:
The Company handled 29,400 carloads in 2010, an increase of approximately 400 carloads over 2009. Aggregate and grain together accounted for 71 percent of volume.

The Company operated 147.4 route miles at the end of 2010, against 177.4 route miles at the end of 2006.

Injury frequency was 1.9 per 200,000 employee hours, the Company's lowest recorded figure.

Cordray Rail Holdings, Inc. does not publish results by subsidiary and the Company does not publish results at all. This notice is the whole of what is published.

blocks.text: Ellery Street bridge deck removed -- Friday 5 November 2010

blocks.body:
The deck of the Company's overhead bridge at Ellery Street, Gridfall, MP 3.1 of the out-of-service Gridfall Subdivision, was removed on Friday 5 November 2010 at the request of the City of Gridfall.

The work was done in one day. Ellery Street was closed between Depot Street and Third Street from 0600 to 1830.

The abutments remain in Company ownership. The Company has no present plan for their removal and no budget for it.

The removal of the deck severs the Gridfall Subdivision at MP 3.1. The Company confirms, as it has confirmed before, that this does not change the status of the subdivision, which has been out of service since 2007.

blocks.text: Grade crossing signal maintenance, Halsey Subdivision -- Monday 19 April 2010

blocks.body:
The Company's signal contractor will perform scheduled maintenance and relamping at eleven public crossings on the Halsey Subdivision between 19 April and 7 May.

Motorists may encounter flaggers and short delays. Signals may be placed in a continuous-flashing condition during testing. A crossing whose signals are flashing is to be treated as occupied whether or not a train is visible.

The work is routine and is required annually.

blocks.text: Track material recovery complete, Marchfield Subdivision -- Friday 18 September 2009

blocks.body:
Recovery of track material from the former Marchfield Subdivision was completed on Friday 14 August 2009.

Approximately eleven miles of 90-pound and 100-pound rail, 30,000 ties, and the associated plates, spikes, bolts and angle bars were removed and sold. Ties not sold were disposed of under permit. Turnouts at Marchfield and at the elevator siding were retained and are in stock at Ardo.

The subgrade, the four bridge structures and all culverts remain in place and remain in Company ownership.

The Company thanks adjoining landowners for access and for their patience with the gates. Fencing questions should be directed to the real estate office at Ardo. The Company is not able to tell anyone where the rail went; it was sold by weight to a scrap buyer and the Company did not follow it.

blocks.text: Embargo continues, Ashkettle Industrial Track -- Friday 22 May 2009

blocks.body:
The embargo on the Ashkettle Industrial Track north of MP 5.0, in effect since 2004, remains in effect.

The condition of the track and of the two timber structures north of MP 5.0 does not permit operation at any speed. The Company has no timetable for restoration of service and no application pending to discontinue it.

Shippers requiring service at Ashkettle should contact the Marketing Department at Ardo. Two shippers at Ashkettle are served by truck to Halsey under arrangements made in 2004 and those arrangements continue.

The Company is aware that several published sources describe the Ashkettle line as closed. It is embargoed, which is a different word, and the difference is not academic to the people who own land along it.

blocks.text: Grade crossing warning devices removed, Marchfield Subdivision -- Monday 27 October 2008

blocks.body:
Flashing light signals and gates at the Quarry Road and Kestrel Road crossings of the former Marchfield Subdivision were removed on Monday 27 October 2008 by the Company's signal contractor.

Crossbucks and advance warning signs at Wessel Street and County Road 9 were removed the same week. The crossing surfaces at all four locations will be removed by the county highway department on its own schedule. Until that work is done, motorists should treat the locations as a rough surface and should not assume the pavement is level.

Salvaged signal material was offered to the county and to the Verity Rail Preservation Society under the Company's surplus material policy. Material taken under that policy is taken as is, with a signed release, and the release is the only record the Company keeps.

blocks.text: Abandonment consummated, Marchfield Subdivision -- Friday 12 September 2008

blocks.body:
Verity Rail Company has consummated the abandonment of its Marchfield Subdivision between Marchfield and Coyne Flats, a distance of 11.6 miles, in Docket No. AB-338 (Sub-No. 4X).

The notice of exemption was filed on Friday 6 June 2008. It became effective on Thursday 11 September 2008. The certificate of consummation was filed on Friday 12 September 2008.

No comments were received during the comment period. No offer of financial assistance was received. No request for a public use condition was received. One request for interim trail use was received, from Verity County, and was withdrawn by the county on Tuesday 2 September 2008.

The last revenue movement over the subdivision took place on Friday 14 March 2008.

blocks.text: Notice of intent to abandon, Marchfield Subdivision -- Monday 9 June 2008

blocks.body:
The Company has given notice of its intent to abandon the Marchfield Subdivision. Notice has been served on the shippers on the line, on the county, on the state, and on the two labour organisations representing affected employees, and has been posted at Marchfield and at Coyne Flats.

Copies of the filing are available for inspection at the general offices at Ardo during business hours, and copies will be mailed on written request.

The Company will respond to written inquiries regarding the filing. The Company will not respond to telephone inquiries regarding the filing. This is not discourtesy; it is that a telephone answer is not a record and this is a proceeding in which everything has to be a record.

blocks.text: Service discontinued, Marchfield Subdivision -- Monday 17 March 2008

blocks.body:
The Company handled its final revenue movement over the Marchfield Subdivision on Friday 14 March 2008.

The movement consisted of three loaded covered hopper cars of corn originating at the Marchfield Farmers Cooperative Association elevator at County Road 9, billed to the river terminal at Steuben. The train left Marchfield at 1042 and cleared the subdivision at 1216.

Marchfield remains an open station on the Halsey Subdivision and is not affected. Grain originating on the subdivision will be handled by truck to Halsey, or by the shipper's own arrangement.

No positions are eliminated. The Marchfield job was worked by the Halsey crew and that crew continues.

The Company thanks the shippers on the subdivision for ninety-seven years of business.

blocks.text: Final scheduled movement, Gridfall Subdivision -- Monday 2 April 2007

blocks.body:
The Company's final scheduled movement over the Gridfall Subdivision left the Depot Street yard at Gridfall on Friday 30 March 2007.

Sixteen positions are eliminated: eleven in the yard, three on the track gang and two clerical. Nine employees have been offered positions on the Ardo Main Line and six have accepted. The Company will assist the remaining employees through the provisions of the applicable agreements.

The yard office at Depot Street, built in 1897, will be secured and retained. The Company has no plan to demolish it.

Track will remain in place. The Company has made no decision regarding salvage.

The Company was asked at the February hearing whether it would sell the line to an operator willing to run it. The answer given then was that the Company would consider a bona fide offer. No offer was received.

blocks.text: Public hearing held, Gridfall Subdivision -- Thursday 15 February 2007

blocks.body:
A public hearing on the Company's abandonment application was held at the Gridfall Armory on Tuesday 13 February 2007. Approximately sixty persons attended. Company representatives answered questions for approximately ninety minutes.

The majority of comment concerned the disposition of the grade crossings at Mill Street and Bracken Lane rather than the discontinuance of service itself.

A transcript is available for inspection at the general offices at Ardo.

blocks.text: Passenger service between Verity Central and Marchfield ends -- Monday 6 March 2006

blocks.body:
The purchase-of-service agreement under which the Company operated weekday and Saturday passenger trains between Verity Central and Marchfield has expired and has not been renewed. The final scheduled trains operated on Saturday 4 March 2006.

The four coaches assigned to the service have been stored at Ardo pending disposition. Crews assigned to the service have been placed under the applicable agreements and no positions are eliminated.

The Company operated the service under contract. The decision not to renew, the loadings study on which it was based, and the consultation that preceded it are matters for Verity County, and inquiries about any of the three should be directed to the county rather than to the Company.

The Company thanks the passengers who used the service and the station volunteers at Marchfield, who were not Company employees and were not paid and did it anyway.

blocks.text: Abandonment application filed, Gridfall Subdivision -- Monday 15 August 2005

blocks.body:
The Company has filed an application for authority to abandon the Gridfall Subdivision between Ardo Junction and Gridfall, a distance of 18.4 miles.

The subdivision handled fewer than 400 carloads in 2004, substantially all of it aggregate from the pit at Quarry Road. The Company's filing states that revenue attributable to the subdivision does not cover the deferred maintenance required to continue operation at present speeds, and that the principal structures require work the traffic will not support.

Notice has been given to shippers, to the state, to affected communities and to the labour organisations representing affected employees.

The filing is a request for authority. It is not a closure and it is not a date. Service continues, on the present schedule, until authority is granted and exercised.

blocks.text: Cordray Rail Holdings completes acquisition -- Monday 15 November 2004

blocks.body:
Verity Rail Company is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Cordray Rail Holdings, Inc.

The Company will continue to operate under its own name, with its own employees, its own operating rules and its own timetable. Curt Neuhaus continues as President and Chief Executive Officer. There is no change to shipper contacts, car order procedure or the terms of existing agreements.

Cordray has asked the Company to complete a review of network performance during 2005.

Company facilities at Gridfall were without commercial power from approximately 4:55 a.m. on Wednesday 11 June 2003 following a fire at the Verity Valley Power & Light substation at Depot and Quarry Road.

Yard lighting, the scale, the car shop and the crossing signals at Mill Street and Bracken Lane were affected. Crossing signals reverted to their fail-safe condition and flagging was provided at both locations.

Train operations continued. The yard office worked on a portable generator brought down from the Ardo shops on Wednesday morning.

Power was restored on Friday afternoon. No Company property was damaged, and no Company employee was injured.

Verity Rail Company has placed this web site in service.

Shippers may view the Company's public timetable summary, a tariff index, the grade crossing inventory and the current charges. The site is best viewed at 800 by 600 in Internet Explorer 5.5 or later.

The Company does not accept car orders through this web site.

This page sets out what the Company did on the Marchfield Subdivision, in what order, and on what dates. It is here because the same eight questions arrive every year and the Company would rather answer them once, accurately, than eight times from memory.

Nothing on this page is legal notice. Notice was given where notice is required to be given and this web site is not one of those places.

head: Date
What happened
rows: The Company applied to take the subdivision out of service. The application was withdrawn the same year after a shipper commitment. Service continued for eleven further years.
Last revenue movement. Three loaded covered hoppers of corn from the elevator at County Road 9, billed to the river terminal at Steuben.
Service formally discontinued. Marchfield remains open on the Halsey Subdivision.
Notice of exemption filed, Docket No. AB-338 (Sub-No. 4X).
Notice served on shippers, the county, the state and the labour organisations. Notices posted at Marchfield and Coyne Flats.
Verity County withdrew its request for interim trail use.
Certificate of consummation filed. The subdivision is abandoned from this date.
Flashing lights and gates removed at Quarry Road and Kestrel Road. Crossbucks removed at Wessel Street and County Road 9.
Corridor conveyed to Verity County. Deed recorded.

blocks.body:
The Company proceeded by [b]notice of exemption[/b] rather than by application. A notice of exemption is available where a line has carried fewer than 50 carloads in each of the two preceding years and no local traffic has moved over it for at least two years, or where the traffic and financial tests are otherwise met. The Company certified that those conditions were satisfied and served the certification on the parties entitled to it.

A notice of exemption is not a hearing. There was no hearing because no party asked for one. The comment period ran from the date of publication to thirty days before the effective date. No comments were filed.

An offer of financial assistance is the mechanism by which any person may offer to buy a line rather than see it abandoned, at a price set by the Board if the parties cannot agree. No offer of financial assistance was made. The Company is sometimes told that it refused an offer. It did not receive one.

items: It ends the Company's obligation to provide common carrier service over the subdivision.
It ends the Company's authority to operate over it.
It releases the corridor from the regulatory condition that kept it whole.

blocks.text: What the abandonment does not do

items: It does not convey land to anybody. Title was unchanged until June 2011.
It does not extinguish an easement, a reversion or a crossing right. Those are matters of state law and of the deed, and some of them on this subdivision go back to conveyances of 1889 and 1910.
It does not make the right of way public. It was private property until 2011 and it is the county's property now.
It does not affect Marchfield, which is on the Halsey Subdivision and is open.

blocks.body:
Four public crossings existed on the subdivision. All four were closed out in October 2008. The Company removed the warning devices and its own signs. The pavement and the approaches belong to the road authority and were the county's to remove or leave.

The county did the surfaces in 2009. The rail and the timber were taken out at Quarry Road and at Kestrel Road and the gaps patched with asphalt. County Road 9 was ground and overlaid. Wessel Street was patched twice.

All four have settled since and all four are humps. That is a county matter and not a Company matter, and the Company notes it with some regret, having had the same argument about the same four locations for thirty years while they were still its own.

[b]The Company no longer maintains anything at any of these locations.[/b] A sign down in the ditch at one of them is not the Company's sign and has not been since 2008.

While the Company held the corridor, it maintained the fences it was obliged to maintain under the original conveyances and it maintained the culverts. It did not mow.

On conveyance in June 2011 those obligations passed to Verity County along with the land. Landowners with a fence question, a drainage question or a gate question should write to the county, and the Company will forward misdirected letters once and then stop, because the forwarding is being done by a person who also does three other jobs.

blocks.text: Questions the Company is actually asked

blocks.body: No.

blocks.text: Could it reopen if somebody bought it?

blocks.body: No. The rail is gone, the ties are gone, the corridor belongs to the county, and the structures were inspected in 2009 and were not good then. This is not a question about willingness.

blocks.text: May I walk on the right of way?

blocks.body: Not while the Company held it. Since June 2011 it is the county's and the answer is the county's to give.

Sold by weight to a scrap buyer in 2009. The Company does not keep records of the onward movement of scrap material and could not trace a particular rail if it wanted to. Date nails and rail brands left on the ground were left on the ground deliberately and the Company has no objection to their being picked up now that the land is not the Company's.

blocks.text: Can I have a copy of the filing?

blocks.body: Yes. Write to the general offices at Ardo and it will be mailed. It is fourteen pages and most of it is a certification and a map.

blocks.text: My father worked on this line. Do you have his record?

blocks.body:
Probably not in a form the Company can find. Personnel records before 1983 came from the predecessor in poor order and were microfilmed in 1991 by a contractor who indexed them by pension number and not by name. The Company will look if you can supply a pension number. It cannot look by name and is sorry about it.

The Verity Rail Preservation Society, which meets at the Marchfield Public Library, holds a conductor's book and several linear feet of paper from the branch and has been more use to people asking this question than the Company has.

blocks.text: Why is this page so flat?

blocks.body:
Because an abandonment is paperwork, and writing it up as anything else would be the Company telling you how to feel about its own decision.

The people who want the other version of it have written it themselves, at length, since 2001, at [url=synth://forums.verityrail.org/]forums.verityrail.org[/url].

[b]If a vehicle is stopped or stalled on a grade crossing, get everyone out of the vehicle and away from the tracks first.[/b] Then telephone the number on the blue and white sign at the crossing and read out the crossing number printed on the sign. That number tells the dispatcher which crossing you are standing at, in seconds, without a description of the road.

The emergency number posted at Company crossings is answered at the Ardo dispatcher's desk, twenty-four hours, by a person. It is not a recording and it is not an answering service. It is one of two desks and if it rings twice it is because the other telephone is also ringing.

blocks.text: If you are stopped on a crossing

items: Get out. Get everyone out. Leave the vehicle.
Walk away from the tracks and toward the train, at an angle of about forty-five degrees. If the train strikes the vehicle, the wreckage goes forward.
Telephone the number on the blue and white sign and give the crossing number.
If there is no sign, telephone the emergency services and tell them the road and the nearest cross street.
Do not go back for anything in the vehicle. This is where people are killed.

blocks.body: Public crossings on Company lines, with warning device and status. Private crossings are not listed and are the responsibility of the landowner under the terms of the crossing agreement.

[i]Inventory reviewed 3 February 2011. Crossing numbers are the numbers on the signs and the numbers the dispatcher reads from. A crossing whose devices have been removed keeps its number on the Company's record for as long as the record exists, which is why a removed crossing still appears in this table.[/i]

blocks.text: Signals that are flashing with no train in sight

blocks.body:
Treat the crossing as occupied and stop. Then telephone the number on the sign and report it.

A signal that activates without a train is usually a shunt fault, damp ballast or a broken bond wire. It is not the signal being clever and it is not a sign that the crossing is out of service. The Company has no way of knowing a signal is behaving this way unless somebody telephones.

The Company received eleven such reports in 2010 and nine of them were the same two crossings in the same wet fortnight.

The right of way is private property. That includes the ballast, the cess, the bridges and the ground between the fences. It includes out-of-service track. The Gridfall Subdivision is out of service, the rail is still in it, and it is still the Company's property and still fenced where it was fenced.

More people are killed on railroad property in this country walking than at grade crossings. That figure is not a Company figure and the Company has no reason to soften it.

Photographers: the road bridges are public and the sightlines are better. See [url=/community]Verity Rail in the Community[/url].

The Company presented grade crossing safety in schools at Ardo, Halsey and Marchfield from 1994 to 2009, and ran a fourth-grade poster contest, the winning posters going on the back of the Company calendar.

The program was suspended in 2009 when the public affairs position was reduced and has not been restored. Schools that would like material should write to Ardo. There are about two hundred sets left in the cupboard and they will not be reprinted.

The Company has employees in four towns and track through six. This page collects the things the Company is asked about that are not shipping and not safety.

[i]This page was last reviewed on Thursday 3 February 2011. The public affairs position that maintained it was reduced in 2009 and the page has been maintained since by the Ardo office as time allows, which has been less time than the page needs.[/i]

The [url=synth://forums.verityrail.org/]Verity Rail Enthusiasts' Forum[/url] at forums.verityrail.org is not a Company web site. It is operated independently, by its own volunteers, on its own hosting, and the views expressed on it are not the views of the Company. Some Company employees post there. They post as themselves and not for the Company, and the Company has never asked them to stop.

The Company does not maintain a historical archive, a photograph collection or a research service. It has not had a person who could answer a historical question since 2009.

[b]Please do not write to the Company for information about the branch lines.[/b] The forum will very likely have it, and will have it in more detail and with better citation than the Company ever did. The Company has itself used the forum twice to settle a question about its own property, which is embarrassing and is also true.

The Verity Rail Preservation Society meets at the Marchfield Public Library and holds the paper. The Company gave them what it could find in 2002 and 2008 and that is now more than the Company has.

Photography from a public road, a public sidewalk or a road bridge is not a Company matter and the Company has no view on it. Company employees have been asked not to move photographers off public ground and generally do not.

The Company does not issue photography permits and has not since 2007. A written request to enter Company property to photograph is made on form VR-51 to the Ardo office, allow thirty days, and is declined in nearly all cases. The exceptions have been for a historical society, for a county assessment, and once for a person documenting a bridge the Company was about to alter.

What the Company asks in return is the thing it has asked for thirty years: stay off the ballast, stay off the bridges, do not stand between the gates, and do not photograph from a crossing you are blocking.

blocks.caption: VR 4412 at Marchfield, shortly after donation in 2002.

blocks.body:
Caboose VR 4412, an International Car Company bay-window car built in 1966, was retired by the Company in 1994 and donated to the Verity Rail Preservation Society in June 2002. It sits on a short length of rail beside the freight house at Marchfield.

The Company retains no interest in the car, no responsibility for it, and no key to it. Questions about opening it are for the Society.

The Company disposes of surplus material by sale, by scrap, or occasionally by transfer to a historical organisation under a signed release. Requests are made in writing to the Ardo office.

The Company does not sell date nails, spikes, lanterns, switch locks, timetables or heralds, and does not have a gift shop. The people who write to ask are not being unreasonable and there is simply nothing to sell them.

Community giving is administered by Cordray Rail Holdings. Requests under $500 are considered at Ardo and are usually answered within a month. Larger requests go to Cordray and take longer.

The Company has given to the volunteer fire departments at Halsey and Coyne Flats every year since 1986, in amounts that will not impress anybody, on the reasoning that they are the people who come when the Company has a problem.

The Company does not sponsor athletic teams and has not since 1999, when it sponsored two and was asked by nine.

The Company printed a wall calendar every year from 1984 to 2008, with photographs sent in by employees and, from 1996, the winning posters from the school safety contest on the back.

The 2009 calendar was not printed. There was no announcement; the print order simply was not placed, and by the time anybody noticed it was March.

The Company has no back stock of calendars. It is asked for them about once a month.
[i]Visitors to this page since April 2004. The counter is a script the Company's first host supplied and it has never been checked against anything.[/i]

entries.author: VerityPulseAI
entries.body: This page has been summarised for accessibility. Summary: Verity Rail Company provides passenger and freight rail service throughout Verity County, including the Ashkettle Branch, with connections at Gridfall Union. The company maintains an active community outreach program and welcomes visitor inquiries. Page last updated 2011. Was this summary helpful?

blocks.body:
[b]The Company is not accepting applications at this time.[/b]

That sentence has been on this page since November 2009 and the Company would rather leave it up and be honest than take it down and collect applications it cannot act on.

[i]This page was last reviewed on Thursday 3 February 2011.[/i]
None.

items: Positions covered by agreement are bulletined internally and go to seniority. Most positions are covered by agreement, which is why the list above says 'internal' three times out of four.

External hiring is by application on form VR-71, mailed, with a medical and a rules examination to follow. The rules examination is not a formality and about a third of candidates fail it the first time.
Seasonal track labor is hired in March and is hard work outdoors in weather. The Company would rather say that plainly than have somebody quit in the second week, which happens anyway.

blocks.body:
The Company has two seniority districts, Ardo and Steuben. The Gridfall district was consolidated into Ardo effective 1 January 2009, having had no assigned positions since April 2007.

Employees who transferred from Gridfall in 2007 retained their dates. Six did. Of those six, four are still with the Company in 2011.

Personnel Office, Verity Rail Company, 1400 Front Street, Ardo. Mark the envelope with the position title if you are answering a bulletin.

The Company will acknowledge a written application and will not keep it on file longer than a year. It has been keeping them since 2009 and the file is now a drawer of people who found other work.

[b]Call the number on the blue and white sign at the crossing and give the crossing number printed on the sign.[/b] That number is answered at the Ardo dispatcher's desk, twenty-four hours. Do not use any number on this page for a crossing emergency. The offices are not staffed at night and the general number goes to a recording after 1700.

The facsimile number above is the current one. Form VR-22 as printed carries the number the Company used before 2007 and the Company is aware of it. The old number is answered by a machine that belongs to somebody else and the Company has apologised to them twice.

Verity Rail Company
1400 Front Street
Ardo

Mark the envelope for the department. An envelope marked only 'Verity Rail' goes to the front desk and the front desk is one person who also weighs the mail.

To the general offices, in writing, marked for the President's office. The Company does not have a press office.

The Company will confirm facts on the record. It does not give background and it does not comment on filings that are pending, which is not evasion but the reason the notice of intent to abandon said what it said about telephone inquiries.

Company notices are placed with the county paper of record, [url=synth://verityledger.com/]the Verity Ledger[/url], which has printed every legal notice the Company has given it since 1983, usually correctly.

Livestock, fire, fence and crop damage claims go in writing to the claims desk at Ardo with the date, the location by road or milepost, and photographs if you have them. An adjuster will come out.

The Company pays claims it owes and does not pay claims it does not owe, and has been consistent enough about both that most people on the line know which theirs is before they write.

Comments on this web site may be sent to webmaster@verityrail.org. The address is read, but not daily, and not by anybody whose job it is.

The comment form that used to be on this page required a browser feature that stopped working and was removed rather than fixed. The Company was quoted a price to rebuild it and did not accept the quotation.

[i]This page was last reviewed on Thursday 3 February 2011.[/i]
